proof:
# Exact compression of integer means of a fractional partition

Let P be a nonempty finite lattice-convex subset of Z^n, meaning
conv(P) intersect Z^n=P, and let w_z>0 for z in P. There is a fractional
partition of these masses into at most 2^n positive classes, each having
an integer barycenter in P. Moreover the positive class barycenters are
the vertices of a lattice polytope with no other lattice points.

This counts CLASS BARYCENTERS, not the original fibers supporting any
class. A class can use arbitrarily many source fibers. In particular the
capacity obstruction in candidate 773c78a48aafd464
does not apply to this different statement.

## 1. A finite attained minimization

For each potential target j in P and source z in P introduce c_jz>=0.
Require

    sum_j c_jz=w_z for every z,
    sum_z (z-j)c_jz=0 for every j.                       (1)

The diagonal array c_zz=w_z, c_jz=0 for j!=z is feasible. The feasible
set is a nonempty compact polytope: each c_jz lies between zero and w_z.
Minimize the linear objective

    E(c)=sum_j |j|^2 m_j,  m_j=sum_z c_jz.              (2)

A minimum is attained. Let V={j:m_j>0} at any minimizer.

## 2. The exact merging argument

Suppose distinct j_1,...,j_r in V and positive numbers lambda_i summing
to one satisfy j=sum_i lambda_i j_i in Z^n, with r>=2. Then j lies in
P by lattice convexity. Choose epsilon>0 with
epsilon lambda_i<=m_(j_i) for every i. Remove the source vector

    epsilon lambda_i c_(j_i,z)/m_(j_i)

from row j_i and add the sum of these vectors to row j. All columns
retain the same total. The removed vector from row j_i has total mass
epsilon lambda_i and first moment epsilon lambda_i j_i. Therefore the
vector added to row j has total mass epsilon and first moment epsilon j.
Every row still satisfies (1), including when j was an existing target.
All entries remain nonnegative. The change in (2) is

    epsilon (|j|^2-sum_i lambda_i |j_i|^2)
      =-epsilon sum_i lambda_i |j_i-j|^2 <0.            (3)

This contradicts minimality. Thus no integer point can be a nontrivial
convex combination of distinct elements of V.

Consequently every point of V is a vertex of conv(V), and

    conv(V) intersect Z^n=V.                            (4)

Indeed a nonvertex of V or an additional lattice point in its convex
hull has precisely a nontrivial convex representation of the excluded
kind, after discarding zero coefficients. No rationality of the weights
or Caratheodory bound is needed.

If p,q in V were distinct with the same parity, (p+q)/2 would be an
integer nontrivial convex combination. Hence the reduction modulo 2 map
is injective on V, proving |V|<=2^n. For n=0 the sole possible target
gives one class directly.

## 3. Application to the intrinsic mixed measure

Let C be as in OC, q=dim_H(S)>=1, and let P be the positive q-dimensional
integer fibers. These are lattice-convex: for any convex combination of
their bases that is an integer j, the Minkowski combination of the source
fibers lies in C_j, is of dimension at least q, and hence has dimension
exactly q by maximality of q. A nonempty compact convex q-dimensional
set has positive finite H_q measure. Thus j is again in P.

Put w_z=H_q(C_z) and obtain the array (1). On the positive fiber C_z,
give class j the constant fractional density c_jz/w_z. These densities
are nonnegative and sum to one. Class j has mass m_j and base first
moment m_j j. The construction is exact for arbitrary real fiber masses.
Lower-dimensional fibers carry zero relevant measure and can be retained
in subsequent closed geometric cells without changing any moment.

The simultaneous convex-cell realization theorem in the companion note
candidate edf02845b3275e8c turns these feasible
class moments into actual polyhedral cells of C, with null pairwise
intrinsic overlaps. Applied here it gives at most 2^n positive-mass convex
subbodies whose union is all of C, and whose TRUE
intrinsic centroids have integer bases in V. Each such centroid belongs
to the original mixed set by convexity. The companion theorem is a
separate proof dependency; this note proves the finite support compression.

The count 2^n is sharp, even before geometric realization. For
P={0,1}^n with all weights positive, a dominated class whose base mean
is j in P must be supported entirely on the source j. To see this,
every coordinate taking the value zero or one at j forces the same
coordinate almost surely in the source, by nonnegativity. Therefore
every vertex needs its own positive class.

No cap-depth guarantee is asserted for the class centroids. In particular
the continuous-dimensional Grunbaum constant does not automatically
apply to a convex subbody equipped with intrinsic mixed measure.
